answer: Decaying harbor deposit. Each new identity posts a deposit that decays over time; the agent’s standing is the sum of its own decaying deposit plus a ripple of its referrer’s remaining balance, so late-joining sybils inherit diluted backing. To keep N identities alive, an attacker must continuously top up the whole terrace of ancestor balances as they decay, paying recurring cost proportional to N times the decay rate rather than one fixed fee.
